Fable-Opus-Unit: bank-demo-fleet-pipeline-p1c/T029-ingest-lineage-rebatch
Fable-Opus-Timeout-Minutes: 30

## Goal

Two things, in order. **(3)** Land the last piece of the T027 ruling in `ingest`. **(5)** Re-batch the six unseen React apps **twice** — once with zero declarations, once with the three T004 install policies declared **once for the fleet** — and publish both, so the coverage report and the runbook can say exactly how far an unseen CRA-era React app gets with nothing declared, and how far with the one operator decision a bank makes once.

Why. Yesterday's batch (T013): 6 unseen apps, 0 proven, all refused at ingest or era-cell. T027 ruled three refusal classes over-strict; T028 landed the era-cell and coverage-report halves — colorme now passes era-cell, flame passes ingest but reads its Express **root** manifest at license-at-pin. What's left is ingest: walking up to the acquisition root for sub-directory frontends, reading the frontend root **by lineage**, and reading the id from the journal. Then the re-batch shows whether the number moves.

### (3) ingest — read `packages/cli/src/operator/ingest.ts` :150-260 (id inference, `acquisitionLaneOf` at :220-229 which exact-matches `.versionless/work/<id>/baseline`, revision from the journal — T023's four gates) and :405-426 (frontend root by manifest PRESENCE today), then `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/notes/T027-react-batch-ruling.md` §3.

- `acquisitionLaneOf` walks UP from the given root to the nearest enclosing `.versionless/work/<id>/baseline`, gated by walking THAT tree and matching the journalled `archiveParity` digest (T023's four gates unchanged: `result === source-bound`, `consentId` present, parity basis present, digest matches).
- Frontend root by **lineage** across the acquisition root and its immediate subdirectories: exactly one manifest declaring react/next/angular is read; zero or several refuse naming every candidate and what each manifest declared. Record `frontendRootBasis`. Never by position.
- Identifier from the journal under the same five gates when `package.json` has no `name`, `idReadFrom` naming it *an operator declaration made at acquire time*. Never a directory name.
- Propagate the frontend root from ingest to analyze, era-cell, plan, apply in `packages/cli/src/operator/run.ts` (`--frontend-root` exists at :154,161) and print both roots in the run record.
- Tests in `operator-ingest.test.ts` (walk-up + gate; lineage read with one/zero/several candidates; id from journal) and `operator-run.test.ts` (both roots printed).

### (5) two-pass re-batch — read `packages/cli/src/operator/batch.ts` (how `--name`, `--apps`, and forwarded flags work; note it forces `VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=offline` ONLY on the publish steps — do NOT set it on the batch itself, install must reach the registry).

- Write `evidence/runs/fleet-batch/t029-react-fleet.json` naming the six BASELINE roots (`.versionless/work/react-{antd-admin-template-v2-0-0,colorme-2019-06-06,coverview-a1470b01,cra-redux-1a06509b,flame-v2-4-0,your-spotify-1-5-0}/baseline` — NO `/client` suffixes, NO per-app declarations).
- **Pass 1**: `batch --apps evidence/runs/fleet-batch/t029-react-fleet.json --out <tmp> --name t029-undeclared --publish --json`. Expected shape (T027, stated in advance): zero of the four T013 codes; every remaining refusal at plan or later; dominated by `install.*-policy-not-declared`.
- **Pass 2**: same, `--name t029-fleet-install-policies`, plus `--allow-remote-tarballs --allow-install-scripts --allow-peer-conflicts` — the three T004 policies, declared once fleet-wide, NOTHING per app. Report verbatim: `refusedByCode`, how many rows reached `install` / `build` / `witness` / `proven`, `defects`, `interventionCount` (must be 0), the coverage report `totals` before and after, old→new trust digest. An npm install that fails on a real 2016–2022 CRA app at Node 24 (node-sass, deprecated peer trees) is a **named refusal or a defect row per the install stage's own contract** — report which; do not fight it per app.
- If a real app exposes a crash/hang, that row is `defect:*` — record it as a finding; do not hand-fix product code except a clearly small, clearly general bug (say what).

Then regenerate census/trust via the pipeline (`--publish` does it; declared dist pack first only if stale). Freeze composite `27741d9c` stable; sealed matrix verbatim.

Budget: 30 minutes. **Land (3) and start pass 1 by minute 12; start the verify chain by minute 20.** If pass 2 cannot finish, publish pass 1 and return `blocked` naming pass 2 — not `partial`. Emit your receipt even if a command is reported not re-run — the harness runs the block after a `completed` receipt.

## File contract

- `packages/cli/src/operator/**`
- `packages/cli/src/cli.ts`
- `packages/cli/test/**`
- `evidence/runs/**`
- `evidence/ingests/**`
- `evidence/trust/current/**`

## Forbidden moves

- Do not write inside `packages/frameworks/react`, `packages/frameworks/angular`, `packages/core/src/migrations`, `packages/core/src/bundlers`, or `packages/core/src/analysis`. Why: sealed under freeze `27741d9c`. If an app needs the adapter widened, that is a finding.
- **Do not run `git stash`, `git checkout -- <path>`, `git reset`, or `git clean`.** Why: the tree holds ~50 uncommitted files from this tranche; T028 stashed/popped them to check a lint warning and the scope guard flagged seven files. A failed pop destroys the tranche.
- Do not set `VERSIONLESS_NETWORK_MODE=offline` on the batch or on `run`. Why: install must reach the registry; only publish steps are offline (batch already does that).
- Do not choose a frontend root by position, take an id from a directory name, follow a redirect, or tune any declaration per app. Why: T027 ruled these per-app tuning by force — the silent manual residue.
- Do not let the coverage report reach `proven` on any run whose stages are not all `ran`. Why: T028's proven bar (charter standing constraint).
- Do not reword an existing refusal message; do not hand-edit anything under `evidence/`. Why: verbatim strings; emitted artifacts only.
- Do not run `vp pack` except once, first, if dist is stale (or via `--publish`). Do not run `vp fmt` repo-wide. Why: provenance subject; 249 pre-existing files.
- Do not describe any app as proven, admitted, or working unless the report row says `proven`. Why: the report is the arbiter.

## Verification

```verify
npm run lint
npm test
npm run trust:verify -- --offline
npm run receipt:verify
node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts refusal-census --verify-only --json
node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts report:coverage --offline --verify-only
node --experimental-strip-types packages/cli/src/cli.ts supported-matrix --offline
node -e "const f=require('./evidence/trust/current/adapter-freeze.json');if(!String(f.freeze.composite).startsWith('27741d9c'))throw new Error('freeze composite moved: '+f.freeze.composite);console.log('FREEZE-COMPOSITE-STABLE')"
git diff --quiet HEAD -- packages/frameworks/react packages/frameworks/angular packages/core/src/migrations packages/core/src/bundlers packages/core/src/analysis && echo FREEZE-INTACT
node -e "const f=require('./evidence/runs/fleet-batch/t029-undeclared/fleet-summary.json');const t=f.totals;if(t.applications!==6)throw new Error('apps '+t.applications);if(t.interventionCount!==0)throw new Error('interventions '+t.interventionCount);const gone=['era-cell.cell-not-declared-for-framework','era-cell.node-major-not-inferable','ingest.revision-not-determined','ingest.identifier-not-determined'];for(const c of gone)if(t.refusedByCode&&t.refusedByCode[c])throw new Error('T013 refusal survived: '+c);const late=new Set(['plan','apply','install','build','witness']);for(const a of f.applications){if(!a.refusal)continue;if(!late.has(a.refusal.stage))throw new Error(a.id+' still refuses at '+a.refusal.stage+' with '+a.refusal.code)}console.log('PASS1 all 6 past era-cell; refusedByCode='+JSON.stringify(t.refusedByCode)+' proven='+t.proven+' defects='+t.defects)"
node -e "const f=require('./evidence/runs/fleet-batch/t029-fleet-install-policies/fleet-summary.json');const t=f.totals;if(t.applications!==6)throw new Error('apps');if(t.interventionCount!==0)throw new Error('interventions');console.log('PASS2 proven='+t.proven+' refusedByCode='+JSON.stringify(t.refusedByCode)+' defects='+t.defects)"
node -e "const r=require('./evidence/trust/current/coverage-report.json');if(r.totals.proven<10)throw new Error('sealed proven fell');for(const row of r.applications){if(row.status!=='proven'||row.provenanceOfStatus!=='run-record')continue;const s=row.stages||[];if(s.length===0||!s.every(x=>x.status==='ran'))throw new Error('proven row with stages not all ran: '+row.id)}console.log('COVERAGE proven='+r.totals.proven+' applications='+r.totals.applications)"
```

`npm test` takes ~150s; green baseline is 2676/2676 (+2 skipped). `npm run trust:verify` WITHOUT `-- --offline` fails by design.

## Blocked permission

If evidence is missing, the contract conflicts with reality, or you need a file outside the contract, return status "blocked" with the question in open_questions instead of improvising. Specifically block, do not improvise, if: any inference T027 forbade would be needed; any row shows `interventionCount > 0` (Phase 1 regression — name app and stage); the registry is unreachable from this host (then a fleet-wide `install.registry-not-reachable` refusal is the honest addition, per T027 — say so and stop); publish moves a sealed number or the freeze composite; or a verify command fails for a cause outside your contract.

164	## 2. Open `engines` range the host satisfies
165	
166	**Applications:** `react-coverview-a1470b01` — `engines.node ">=24.x"`, host running 24;
167	`react-ant-design-pro-v5-2-0` — `engines.node ">=10.0.0"`, host 24, and its own CI matrix reads

170	### Ruling: a satisfaction check is a **reading**; a floor pick is a **guess**. Both cases decide the same way, and neither yields an era.
171	
172	T008 §5(b) forbade taking the floor of an open range as the authored era, and that ruling stands
173	untouched. The line is not about which range or which host. It is about **which field the reading
174	populates**:
175	
176	| act | field populated | value | verdict |
177	|---|---|---|---|
178	| floor of `>=10.0.0` | `era.major` | `10` | **guess** — answers the era question with a number the range does not state |
179	| floor of `>=24.x` | `era.major` | `24` | **guess** — the floor coinciding with the host makes it look right; it is the same act |
180	| `24 ∈ [24, ∞)` | `runtime.satisfiedByDeclaredRange` | `true` | **reading** — answers a different question, yields a boolean, extracts no major |
181	| `24 ∈ [10, ∞)` | `runtime.satisfiedByDeclaredRange` | `true` | **reading** — same |
182	
183	**No number is ever taken out of a range and put in an era field.** If a range ever populates
184	`era.major`, it is a guess; if it populates `runtime.satisfiedByDeclaredRange`, it is a reading.
185	That is the whole line, and it is checkable by a test rather than by taste.

246	- **flame's acquisition root carries its own `package.json`** (name `flame`, an Express server;
247	  no react, no react-scripts). `ingest.ts:405-407` therefore reads `frontendRoot = '.'` and the

356	## 4. FINDING — the acquisition refusal on three candidates
357	
358	The T013 receipt reads: *"Three further candidates … refused ACQUISITION with 'Acquisition response
359	status differs' (https-transaction.ts:105, the two-stream byte-identity guard) on the three largest
360	archives."* **Three of the four claims in that sentence are wrong, and the disk proves it.**
361	
362	### What the guard at that line is
363	
364	`https-transaction.ts:102-118` is a **single-response status check**: anything other than HTTP 200
365	is rejected, with `property` set to `redirect-status` for 3xx and `non-200-status` otherwise, both
366	carrying the message `Acquisition response status differs`. It compares one response against the
367	constant 200. It is not a comparator of two streams.
368	
369	The two-stream byte-identity guard is elsewhere and has its own code: `acquire.ts:497-522` fetches
370	the archive twice and refuses `acquire.archive-streams-differ` on a sha256 mismatch. It never ran.
371	
372	### What actually happened, read off disk
373	
374	`persistAcceptedResponse` (`https-transaction.ts:34-52`) creates `transaction.durableRoot` on the
375	**first accepted response**. For all three candidates:
376	
377	```
378	.versionless/cache/react-answer-v2-0-2-source/            -> archive/ (empty), no transaction/
379	.versionless/cache/react-casdoor-v3-154-3-source/         -> archive/ (empty), no transaction/
380	.versionless/cache/react-emoji-search-style-import-source/-> archive/ (empty), no transaction/
381	evidence/ingests/react-{answer,casdoor,emoji-search-*}/   -> empty directories
382	```
383	
384	No durable root, no journal, no `attempt.json`, no archive bytes. **Zero responses were ever
385	accepted**, so the failure fired on the *first* request of each acquisition — `GET
386	https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{name}`, `acquire.ts:429`, purpose `repository identity`. The
387	archives were never requested. Size, chunked transfer and the archive cap are all irrelevant: no
388	archive was touched. And `ahfarmer/emoji-search` is a small tutorial application, which by itself
389	refutes "the three largest".
390	
391	The six successes ran in two concurrent waves (identical `startedAt`: four at
392	`21:36:05.98`, two at `21:37:42.10`), 35 accepted responses in total, ~23 of them to
393	`api.github.com`. The three failures sit inside those same waves.
394	
395	### Is it an integrity signal?
396	
397	**On the evidence available: unknowable, and that is the actual finding.** `state.observations`
398	lives in memory (`transaction.ts:16-24`, `https-transaction.ts:91-101`) and is written only into a
399	record that a successful acquisition produces (`acquire.ts:633-653`). A refused acquisition writes
400	nothing. So the observed status code, the URL, the purpose and the response headers were all
401	discarded, and nobody — the worker, the PM, or this Judge — can say whether those three were 301
402	(`apache/incubator-answer` is a repository that was renamed, and the GitHub API answers a renamed
403	repository with 301), 403/429 (an unauthenticated secondary rate limit, which concurrent waves
404	provoke), or 404. Three different operator responses, one indistinguishable failure string.

406	**A refusal that names no basis is exactly what this repository refuses to accept from an
407	application. It cannot accept it from itself.**

429	   - 403/429 → `acquire.rate-limited`, carrying `retry-after`, `x-ratelimit-remaining` and
430	     `x-ratelimit-reset` when present. The headers are already observed; only their recording is
431	     new.
432	4. **Serialize acquisitions.** The concurrent waves are visible in the timestamps and are the most
433	   plausible provocation of a secondary limit. Serializing costs seconds on a six-application

438	
439	`acquire.archive-streams-differ` is correct and stays. Its record is currently lost the same way:
440	the refusal fires before `source.json` is written, so both sha256s vanish. It must carry, in the

# T027 — Ruling on the four refusal classes of the first React coverage batch

Judge, read-only. 2026-08-17. Board: `docs/goals/bank-demo-fleet-pipeline/state.yaml`.
Predecessor ruling: `notes/T008-phase1-gate.md` §5. Posture: `packages/cli/src/operator/analyze.ts:82`.

> "Detection reads declarations. Nothing here establishes that this application installs,
> compiles, builds, or behaves as it did on its era toolchain."

A reading names its basis; a guess does not. Everything below turns on **which field a reading is
allowed to populate**, not on how confident anyone is.

---

## 0. What the batch actually established

`evidence/runs/fleet-batch/t013a-undeclared/fleet-summary.json`: 6 applications, 0 proven,
6 refused, 0 defects, `interventionCount 0`, 6538 ms. Coverage held at the sealed 10
(`evidence/trust/current/coverage-report.json` totals `{21, 10, 2, 8, 1}`).

The pipeline is legible and not admitting. Four of the six refusals fire at stage 2 (`ingest`) or
stage 4 (`era-cell`) of nine — i.e. **before the pipeline does anything that could be wrong**.
That is the shape of a pipeline whose admission gates are stricter than its own sealed proofs, and
the precedent proves it: `evidence/runs/operator-flows/lane-install-build.json` records the
papercups lane **installed and built at host `node v24.15.0`**, with `handAuthoredFilesForThisApplication: 0`.
The six sealed React cells are migrated-lane proofs at host Node 24. The era-cell stage refuses an
application for not declaring an era that the sealed proofs never read.

### A fifth thing the batch established that the receipt did not name

`packages/trust/src/coverage-report.ts:183-219` (`applyInterventionRule`) reaches `proven` on
`outcome === 'proceeded'` **plus** a harness count of zero, and reads nothing else. It does not
read `stages`, though its own doc comment at :113-118 says the stage rows exist so "the corpus
conformance admission path reads them to refuse a run that proceeded without every stage running".

Two other surfaces hold the harder bar:

- `packages/cli/src/operator/intervention-count.ts:324-336` — `classifyTerminal` returns `proven`
  only when `exitCode === 0` **and** every stage row reads `ran`; otherwise `defect:stages-not-all-run`.
- `packages/core/src/corpus/conformance.ts:749-753` — admission requires
  `terminalClassification === 'proven'`, `interventions.count === 0`, and `stages.every(status === 'ran')`.

So the **weakest** of the three bars is the one sitting on the oracle's own instrument. Today the
hole is latent: no unseen application reaches `proceeded`, so nothing exercises it. Every ruling
below moves applications past stage 4, which makes it live. If T028 widens admission without
closing this, the very next batch can move the proven count from 10 to 14 on applications that
never installed, never built and were never witnessed — the charter's named misfire, laundered
through a derivation. **This is deliverable (0) of T028 and it is not optional.**

It is a tightening, not a widening: it cannot create a proven row, only refuse one. Every current
run-record row is `refused`, so the regenerated report must be numerically identical.

---

## 1. React app declaring NO Node era anywhere, React lineage publishing no cell registry

**Applications:** `react-antd-admin-template-v2-0-0` (react-scripts 3.4.1, no `.nvmrc`, no
`engines`, no `.github`, no Dockerfile), `react-colorme-2019-06-06` (react-scripts 0.8.4, same).
Verified by reading both trees.

**Code path:** `era-cell.ts:1007-1010` consults the tree's sources only when neither `--node` nor a
published cell settled the era; `readNodeMajorSources` returns `[]` for these two; `:1058-1064`
refuses `era-cell.cell-not-declared-for-framework`.

### Ruling: **the refusal as written is over-reach. Proceed — but not as a "host-runtime fallback".**

The refusal conflates two different questions under one field:

1. *Which toolchain era was this application authored for?* — an era claim.
2. *Which runtime will the lane this pipeline composes be installed and built in?* — a fact about
   what the pipeline is about to do.

`run` never builds a baseline. `run.ts:440-446` calls `runLaneWitness` with **no** `baselineBuild`,
so `witness.ts:56-72` runs the migrated lane alone. There is no parity comparison in the chain, and
therefore no place where question (1) is load-bearing today. Question (2) has a determinate answer
the pipeline reads off itself: the install and build stages run the lane in **this process's
runtime**, and `lane-install-build.json` records a lane of exactly this composition installing 428
packages and producing 11 build outputs at `v24.15.0`.

Refusing (2) because (1) is unanswerable is the stage declining to state a fact it possesses
because a different fact is absent. That is not conservatism; it is a category error with a
refusal string attached.

Option (b) in the packet is right in substance and wrong in framing. "Proceed on the host runtime"
sounds like a fallback — something taken because nothing better was available. It is not. The
runtime the lane runs in is not a fallback for the era; it is the answer to a different question
that was never asked out loud.

### What the record must say, exactly

`EraCellRecord.required` splits into two named determinations. Neither may borrow the other's field.

```
required: {
  cell: 'react-vite-lane',
  cellSource: 'inferred',
  cellBasis: 'the react lineage publishes no target-cell registry, so no cell is read for it. The
              cell named here is the lane this pipeline composes: the plan and apply stages write a
              Vite lane, and the install and build stages run it in the runtime recorded below.',

  runtime: {
    major: 24,
    version: 'v24.15.0',
    source: 'inferred',
    readFrom: 'the process this stage is running in — the runtime the install and build stages will
               run the lane in',
    basis: 'evidence/runs/operator-flows/lane-install-build.json records a lane of this composition
            installing 428 packages and building 11 outputs at node v24.15.0 on darwin-arm64.',
    claim: 'the migrated lane will be installed and built in this runtime'
  },

  era: {
    outcome: 'not-read',
    declared: null,
    readFrom: null,
    consultedSources: [ /* every source, each with text and majors, including the absent ones */ ],
    claim: 'nothing in this tree names the toolchain era its authors used, and this stage read none'
  }
}
```

**`consultedSources` must list every source that was looked for, including the absent ones**, each
as `{ source, text: null, majors: null, present: false }`. Today `readNodeMajorSources` returns
only what exists, so an application with nothing declared produces an empty array indistinguishable
from a stage that did not look. The refusal string currently carries that list in prose
(".nvmrc, .node-version, package.json#volta.node, .tool-versions, any Dockerfile* FROM a node
image, any .github/workflows node-version, or package.json#engines.node"); once the stage proceeds
there is no refusal string, so the list has to live in the record or it is lost.

Three `notEstablished` lines, verbatim, added to `ERA_CELL_NOT_ESTABLISHED`:

- `The runtime named here is the runtime the lane this pipeline composes will be installed and built in. It is not the era this application was authored for: nothing here establishes which toolchain its authors used.`
- `An era recorded as not-read states that no declaration in this tree named exactly one Node major that this stage reads. It is not a statement that the application has no era, and it is not a statement that the runtime below is that era.`
- `Nothing here establishes that this application installs, compiles, builds, or behaves in the runtime named above. The install and build stages are where that is attempted, and their records are where it is stated.`

### What survives, and what the code keeps

`era-cell.cell-not-declared-for-framework` is **not deleted**. Its condition narrows to: the
lineage publishes no target-cell registry **and** this pipeline composes no lane of its own for
that lineage — i.e. there is no runtime to read either. It stays in the census with its string
verbatim (T004's rule: a refusal is not an occasion to reword a sealed string). Census coupling
applies: `refusal-census.json` moves, the coverage report embeds it, `trust:verify` re-derives it.

### The baseline / parity question, answered even though it is not live

Asked: must a baseline era build also run at host, refuse separately, or run and record
`baseline-built-at-host-not-era`?

**Refuse separately, with its own code, non-halting for the migrated lane.**
`era-cell.baseline-era-not-read` (stage `era-cell`, origin `pipeline`), recorded on the era-cell
row and surfaced by whichever stage would have built the baseline — never halting the migrated
lane, because the migrated lane's runtime is known.

Building a baseline at host and labelling it `baseline-built-at-host-not-era` is admissible **only
if that string bounds the parity claim itself** — i.e. the witness record's own outcome sentence
carries it, not a footnote — because a parity witness whose baseline was built on a runtime the
authors never used is comparing the migration against an artefact of the pipeline's own choosing.
The moment that string has to ride on every downstream parity claim, the separate refusal is
cheaper and clearer. A parity comparison whose baseline was not built at its era may say only:
"the migrated lane and a baseline lane built in the same host runtime were replayed and compared;
no claim is made that the baseline is the artefact this application's toolchain produced."

---

## 2. Open `engines` range the host satisfies

**Applications:** `react-coverview-a1470b01` — `engines.node ">=24.x"`, host running 24;
`react-ant-design-pro-v5-2-0` — `engines.node ">=10.0.0"`, host 24, and its own CI matrix reads
`[12.x, 14.x]` (T008 §5 read this off disk).

### Ruling: a satisfaction check is a **reading**; a floor pick is a **guess**. Both cases decide the same way, and neither yields an era.

T008 §5(b) forbade taking the floor of an open range as the authored era, and that ruling stands
untouched. The line is not about which range or which host. It is about **which field the reading
populates**:

| act | field populated | value | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| floor of `>=10.0.0` | `era.major` | `10` | **guess** — answers the era question with a number the range does not state |
| floor of `>=24.x` | `era.major` | `24` | **guess** — the floor coinciding with the host makes it look right; it is the same act |
| `24 ∈ [24, ∞)` | `runtime.satisfiedByDeclaredRange` | `true` | **reading** — answers a different question, yields a boolean, extracts no major |
| `24 ∈ [10, ∞)` | `runtime.satisfiedByDeclaredRange` | `true` | **reading** — same |

**No number is ever taken out of a range and put in an era field.** If a range ever populates
`era.major`, it is a guess; if it populates `runtime.satisfiedByDeclaredRange`, it is a reading.
That is the whole line, and it is checkable by a test rather than by taste.

`nodeMajorsOfDeclaration` (`era-cell.ts:339-366`) is **not touched**. Its `null` for an open lower
bound is the reading/guessing line drawn in code and T008 §5(b)-2 said so. The satisfaction check
is a new, separate function that never feeds the era field.

`>=24.x` on Node 24 is the more dangerous of the two precisely because the floor is the host: a
floor rule would produce the right number here and the wrong number on ant-design-pro, and a rule
that is right by coincidence is not a rule. ant-design-pro is the proof and it is already on the
record: it declares `>=10.0.0` and its authors ran 12 and 14. **The satisfaction check would return
`true` for a runtime (24) that neither of the majors the application's own CI names.** The record
must therefore carry both readings side by side and must not let one imply the other:

```
runtime: {
  major: 24,
  declaredRange: '>=10.0.0',
  declaredRangeSource: 'package.json#engines.node',
  satisfiedByDeclaredRange: true,
  claim: 'the compatibility range this application declares admits the runtime the lane will run in.
          The range names no era and no major was read from it.'
},
era: { outcome: 'not-read', consultedSources: [ ... including '.github/workflows/ci.yml#node_version
       reads [12.x, 14.x], naming 2 major lines (12, 14)' ... ] }
```

`notEstablished`, verbatim:

- `A declared compatibility range that admits this runtime is a satisfied constraint. It states that the application claims to work on a set of runtimes that includes this one; it names no era, and no Node major was read out of it.`
- `Satisfaction of a declared range is not corroborated by anything else this tree says. Where other sources name majors, they are listed above with what each literally says, and this stage picks from none of them.`

### The one new refusal this ruling adds

If the tree declares a range and the runtime the lane will run in is **outside** it, that is a
contradiction the pipeline is about to walk into, and it is read rather than assumed:

`era-cell.declared-range-excludes-the-lane-runtime` — *"Era cell: this application declares
`engines.node <RANGE>` in `<SOURCE>`, and the runtime the install and build stages would run the
lane in is Node `<MAJOR>` (`<VERSION>`), which that range does not admit. The lane is not installed
in a runtime the application's own manifest excludes; declare the runtime with `--node <major>` if
the range is stale, or provide a runtime the range admits."*

This is strictly a new refusal (nothing reaches it today) and it is the honest half of the same
reading: a check that can only ever answer "yes" is not a check.

---

## 3. Mechanical — sub-directory frontends and a manifest with no `name`

**Applications:** `react-flame-v2-4-0`, `react-your-spotify-1-5-0` (both refused
`ingest.revision-not-determined`), `react-cra-redux-1a06509b` (`ingest.identifier-not-determined`).

### 3a. Why they actually refused — the receipt's diagnosis is one step short

`evidence/runs/fleet-batch/t013a-react-fleet.json` lists flame and your_spotify with
`"root": ".versionless/work/<id>/baseline/client"`. `acquisitionLaneOf` (`ingest.ts:220-229`)
matches exactly `.../.versionless/work/<id>/baseline`; a `/client` suffix matches nothing, so
`readAcquisitionJournal` returns `null` and the T023 seam is never consulted.

Two facts that decide the shape of the fix, read off disk:

- **flame's acquisition root carries its own `package.json`** (name `flame`, an Express server;
  no react, no react-scripts). `ingest.ts:405-407` therefore reads `frontendRoot = '.'` and the
  whole pipeline would analyse the *server*.
- **your_spotify's root carries no manifest**, and `client/` and `server/` both do, so
  `manifestBearingSubdirectories` returns two and `:417-423` refuses
  `ingest.frontend-root-ambiguous`.

So the `/client` roots in the manifest were not a mistake — they were the only way past
`frontend-root-ambiguous` and past the server-manifest shadow. The operator paid for it by losing
the journal. That is a **structural** problem: one `appRoot` is being asked to be two things at
once — the unit of provenance (the acquired tree the journal vouches for) and the unit of
composition (the directory carrying the frontend manifest).

### Ruling: three changes, all readings, all gated.

**(i) Walk up to the acquisition root for the journal — yes, with a hard gate.**
`acquisitionLaneOf` may walk up from `sourceRoot` to the nearest enclosing
`.versionless/work/<id>/baseline`. The honesty condition is *not* "the subdir is inside the tree" —
that is a path fact and paths are cheap. The condition is the same parity gate that already exists,
applied to the right tree:

- the **enclosing acquisition tree** is walked and its `normalizedManifestSha256` compared against
  the journal's `archiveParity.normalizedManifestSha256` (`ingest.ts:320-326`). Mismatch → the
  existing `ingest.acquisition-journal-does-not-match-the-tree`, message extended to say which tree
  was walked;
- the four existing gates (`result === 'source-bound'`, a `consentId`, `archiveMatchesGitTree &&
  archivesByteIdentical`, a 40-hex revision) are unchanged;
- the record states the relationship rather than implying it, in `commitShaReadFrom`:
  `evidence/ingests/<id>/source.json (consent <id>; result source-bound; archive reconciled against
  the published Git tree and byte-identical across two streams; the journalled manifest <digest> is
  the digest of the enclosing acquisition tree at <root>, which this stage walked; the ingested
  frontend <root>/client is a subpath of that tree)`.

This is reading the pipeline's own consent-journalled receipt — the same act T008 §7 already ruled
honest — applied to the tree the journal is actually about.

**(ii) Read the frontend root by lineage, not by manifest presence.**
`manifestBearingSubdirectories` counts `package.json` files. Extend the candidate set to the
acquisition root **and** its immediate subdirectories, and read each candidate's manifest for a
lineage the `analyze` stage recognises (react / next / angular, via `declaredDependencies`).
Exactly one candidate declaring a lineage → **read**, with the basis recorded. Zero or more than
one → refuse, naming every directory considered and what each manifest declared.

- flame: root declares no lineage, `client/` declares react → one → `client`.
- your_spotify: `client/` declares react, `server/` does not → one → `client`.
- The other four: root declares react → `.`, unchanged.

Record: `frontendRootSource: 'read'`, plus a new `frontendRootBasis` naming **every** directory
considered and each one's reading — `"<root> declares no framework this stage reads; client/
declares react ^18.2.0 (dependencies.react); server/ declares no framework this stage reads"`.
`--frontend-root` remains the declaration that overrides it, unchanged.

This is a reading with a stated basis and it refuses on ambiguity. It is not "pick the first".

**(iii) The frontend root must propagate to every stage that composes.**
Today `run.ts:381-446` hands `declarations.appRoot` to `analyze`, `era-cell`, `plan` and `apply`,
and only `license-at-pin` (`:388`) honours `ingest.frontendRoot`. With (ii) in place and the
manifest pointing at baseline roots, `analyze`/`plan` would still read flame's Express server and
refuse the React admission string at stage 5. The ingest stage's frontend reading is made once and
used by every downstream stage: **acquisition root** is the unit of provenance (journal, revision,
licence, tree parity); **frontend root** is the unit of composition (analyze, era-cell, plan,
apply, install, build). The run record must print both, so a reader can see which tree each stage
read. Without (iii), (i) and (ii) buy a later refusal and nothing else.

### 3b. The identifier — yes, from the journal, with the source named honestly

`react-cra-redux-1a06509b`'s `package.json` declares no `name` (verified). The current refusal is
right about the thing it refuses: *"The directory it happens to sit in is not an identity."*
Reading the lane directory name would be exactly that, and stays forbidden.

Reading the **journal** is a different act. `acquire.ts:243-253` refuses without `--id`; the
identifier in `evidence/ingests/<id>/source.json` is an operator declaration made under a named
consent and journalled by the pipeline. Reading it back is reading a recorded declaration.

Conditions: it passes the **same four gates plus the tree-digest gate** as the revision — a journal
that does not bind a source, carries no consent, carries no parity basis, or is not about these
bytes yields no identifier either, and `ingest.identifier-not-determined` stands. And the record
must not launder the provenance:

```
id: 'react-cra-redux-1a06509b',
idSource: 'read',
idReadFrom: 'evidence/ingests/react-cra-redux-1a06509b/source.json (consent VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10),
             where it was declared by an operator with --id at acquire time. This stage read the
             journal, not the application: package.json declares no name and this stage read none.'
```

`notEstablished`, verbatim: `An identifier read from an acquisition journal is the identifier an
operator declared when the source was fetched. The application itself declares none, and nothing
here establishes that the two would agree.`

### 3c. `run --frontend-root` exists; a fleet-wide one is per-app tuning

It exists: `run.ts:154` lists `--frontend-root` under `ingest`, `:161` under `license-at-pin`.
`batch` forwards every non-own flag to every application unchanged (`flows.ts:1341-1344`;
`own = ['--apps','--publish','--name']`).

**A fleet-wide `--frontend-root client` is not a declaration about the fleet — it is per-app tuning
applied by force.** Four of these six carry their manifest at the root, and
`ingest.declared-frontend-root-carries-no-manifest` (`ingest.ts:398-404`) would refuse all four.
It converts three refusals into four different refusals. The frontend root is a property of each
tree, so either the pipeline reads it (ruling (ii)) or the operator declares it per application —
and per-application declaration is the thing T008 §5 named as **silent manual residue that passes
the intervention gate**, because a declaration in the first invocation costs zero interventions by
construction. Reading it is the only answer that keeps the gate meaningful. Do **not** add a
per-application declarations slot to the batch manifest in T028; if a tree genuinely needs one
later, it is a runbook line, not a pipeline default.

---

## 4. FINDING — the acquisition refusal on three candidates

The T013 receipt reads: *"Three further candidates … refused ACQUISITION with 'Acquisition response
status differs' (https-transaction.ts:105, the two-stream byte-identity guard) on the three largest
archives."* **Three of the four claims in that sentence are wrong, and the disk proves it.**

### What the guard at that line is

`https-transaction.ts:102-118` is a **single-response status check**: anything other than HTTP 200
is rejected, with `property` set to `redirect-status` for 3xx and `non-200-status` otherwise, both
carrying the message `Acquisition response status differs`. It compares one response against the
constant 200. It is not a comparator of two streams.

The two-stream byte-identity guard is elsewhere and has its own code: `acquire.ts:497-522` fetches
the archive twice and refuses `acquire.archive-streams-differ` on a sha256 mismatch. It never ran.

### What actually happened, read off disk

`persistAcceptedResponse` (`https-transaction.ts:34-52`) creates `transaction.durableRoot` on the
**first accepted response**. For all three candidates:

```
.versionless/cache/react-answer-v2-0-2-source/            -> archive/ (empty), no transaction/
.versionless/cache/react-casdoor-v3-154-3-source/         -> archive/ (empty), no transaction/
.versionless/cache/react-emoji-search-style-import-source/-> archive/ (empty), no transaction/
evidence/ingests/react-{answer,casdoor,emoji-search-*}/   -> empty directories
```

No durable root, no journal, no `attempt.json`, no archive bytes. **Zero responses were ever
accepted**, so the failure fired on the *first* request of each acquisition — `GET
https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{name}`, `acquire.ts:429`, purpose `repository identity`. The
archives were never requested. Size, chunked transfer and the archive cap are all irrelevant: no
archive was touched. And `ahfarmer/emoji-search` is a small tutorial application, which by itself
refutes "the three largest".

The six successes ran in two concurrent waves (identical `startedAt`: four at
`21:36:05.98`, two at `21:37:42.10`), 35 accepted responses in total, ~23 of them to
`api.github.com`. The three failures sit inside those same waves.

### Is it an integrity signal?

**On the evidence available: unknowable, and that is the actual finding.** `state.observations`
lives in memory (`transaction.ts:16-24`, `https-transaction.ts:91-101`) and is written only into a
record that a successful acquisition produces (`acquire.ts:633-653`). A refused acquisition writes
nothing. So the observed status code, the URL, the purpose and the response headers were all
discarded, and nobody — the worker, the PM, or this Judge — can say whether those three were 301
(`apache/incubator-answer` is a repository that was renamed, and the GitHub API answers a renamed
repository with 301), 403/429 (an unauthenticated secondary rate limit, which concurrent waves
provoke), or 404. Three different operator responses, one indistinguishable failure string.

**A refusal that names no basis is exactly what this repository refuses to accept from an
application. It cannot accept it from itself.**

### Smallest honest widening

The 200-only gate **stays**. Nothing below relaxes it; comparing bodies when statuses differ is not
even applicable here, because at the point of failure there is one response and no body.

1. **Persist the observations on refusal.** Write `evidence/ingests/<id>/attempt.json` with
   `result: 'refused'` and the full `observations` array (`method`, `url`, `purpose`, `attempt`,
   `status`, `headersObserved`, `bodyBytes`, `acceptedResponse`) plus the `AcquisitionFailure`'s
   `stage`/`property`/`expected`/`observed`. This is the whole fix for legibility and it changes no
   gate.
2. **Carry the status and the URL into the refusal string.** `acquire.response-status-differs`:
   *"Acquire: `GET <url>` (`<purpose>`) answered `<status>` and this transport accepts 200 only.
   `<n>` responses had been accepted before it. No byte was read from a response this stage did not
   accept."*

   anything.**

     unfollowed** (`redirectsAllowed: false` is a declared property of the transaction at
     `acquire.ts:583` and must stay: following a redirect would fetch a repository the operator did
     not name). The operator declares the new `owner/name`.
   - 403/429 → `acquire.rate-limited`, carrying `retry-after`, `x-ratelimit-remaining` and
     `x-ratelimit-reset` when present. The headers are already observed; only their recording is
     new.
4. **Serialize acquisitions.** The concurrent waves are visible in the timestamps and are the most
   plausible provocation of a secondary limit. Serializing costs seconds on a six-application
   fleet and removes a whole class of unexplained refusal. A bank's fleet is larger, so this
   matters more there, not less.

`acquire.archive-streams-differ` is correct and stays. Its record is currently lost the same way:
the refusal fires before `source.json` is written, so both sha256s vanish. It must carry, in the
message and in the refused `attempt.json`, **both streams' sha256 and byte counts, the commit sha,
and the URL fetched twice** — because "the two streams differ" without the two digests is an
assertion, and this repository's whole posture is that an assertion is not a reading.

### `react-mycrypto` — one sentence, as asked

`ingest.acquisition-journal-does-not-match-the-tree` on mycrypto is an **honest integrity reading**,
not a bug: the baseline was acquired at 18:06 and carries `dist/web/` written at 18:11–18:12 plus
an installed `node_modules`, and since `workspacePathsBelow` (`analyze.ts:361-374`) skips
`node_modules` and `.git` but **walks `dist`**, a work area that was built in place no longer walks
to the journalled digest `30a28d52…` — which is precisely what the gate exists to catch. (Worth one
message improvement, not a gate change: the refusal should say *how* the tree differs — files
added, removed, changed — so an operator can tell "I built in this work area" from "these are not
the bytes that were fetched".)

> With zero declarations, **0 of 6** CRA-era React applications proceed past `era-cell` today; after
> T028 the expected count is **6**, and the expected first refusal stage for the rest is **`install`**
> — the three declared npm policies (`--allow-remote-tarballs`, `--allow-install-scripts`,
> `--allow-peer-conflicts`), which a bank operator answers **once for the fleet** rather than once
> per application.
